system.name: Cross-Environment Cooperation (CEC)
system.one_liner: Self-play RL on a large distribution of procedurally generated environments, yielding agents that coordinate zero-shot with new partners on new problems.

content.variant_note: two training regimes drawn with identical geometry (agent, partners, environments) with the many/one quantities swapped, followed by a verdict table
content.argues: Training with one partner across many environments, not many partners in one environment, gives zero-shot coordination with new partners and new environments; PBT fails on novel environments.
content.subject: Training setups of PBT and CEC as a learning agent with its partners and environments, and a table of which coordination conditions each succeeds in.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw the two training regimes with identical geometry (agent left, partners above, environments below) and swap only the many / one glyphs, using overlapping avatars for a population and an offset screenshot stack for a distribution; then close with a small tick-and-cross table over the generalisation conditions so the contrast ends in a verdict.
lessons.suits: Papers that argue a change in the training distribution (data, partners, tasks) and can state the result as which generalisation conditions succeed or fail.

evidence: By training agents in self-play on a large distribution of environments
agents develop the ability to coordinate with novel partners and novel problems
prior work which suggests self-play is insufficient for learning general norms for cooperation

summary: The paper trains cooperative agents by self-play on a huge distribution of procedurally generated environments (Cross-Environment Cooperation, CEC) and shows that they coordinate zero-shot with new partners and new problems. Figure 1 is a three-column contrast. On the left, Population-Based Training: a green learning-agent robot trains with many partners (blue, red and orange robots) on one environment screenshot. In the middle, CEC: the same agent trains with one blue partner on a stack of many layouts. On the right, an Evaluation table lists three conditions (novel partners, novel environments, both) with emoji ticks and crosses: PBT fails on novel environments, CEC succeeds in all three. It is a flat Google Slides drawing with robot icons, game screenshots, thin arrows and dashed dividers.
summary_zh: 对比图：左栏群体训练（PBT）让学习智能体与多个伙伴在单一环境中训练，中栏跨环境合作（CEC）让它与单一伙伴在大量环境中训练；右栏评估表用对勾和叉号表明，PBT 在新环境中协作失败，CEC 在三种情形下都能零样本协作。
notes: Prior label side-by-side-contrast / paired-lanes kept; actor-interaction added for the cast of agent, partners and environments. Palette hexes are read off the bitmaps (approximate) because the SVG fills are only black. The panel text is outlined, so the digest lists no strings except the emoji.
